newsitem.title: USA: WPS Resources chairman to retire in June.
newsitem.headline: WPS Resources chairman to retire in June.

text.p: WPS Resources Corp on Thursday confirmed that Daniel Bollom, its chairman and chief executive officer, planned to retire at the end of June.

A spokesman for the Green Bay, Wisconsin-based utility holding company said Larry Weyers, its current president and chief operating officer, will become chief executive, although the timeframe has yet to be announced.
"It could be earlier (than June 30), but there have been no announcements," Frank Kicsar, corporate secretary of WPS, told Reuters.

News of Bollom's retirement comes at a time when WPS, the parent of Wisconsin Public Service Corp, is dealing with problems at its Kewaunee nuclear power plant, which was taken out of service in September for scheduled refueling and maintenance.

Earlier this week, the company said Kewaunee was not expected to resume operations until at least mid-June because repairs to the plant's steam generators were taking longer than expected. It was originally expected to restart by March.
Kewaunee is jointly owned by Wisconsin Public Service Corp, Madison Gas & Electric Co and WPL Holdings Inc's Wisconsin Power & Light Co.
The partners estimated the additional repairs would cost between $4.5 million and $10 million.
The co-owners are also considering whether to replace the steam generators at Kewaunee, a project that would cost an estimated $89 million, WPS said.
"No decision on whether to replace the steam generators has been made at this time," Kicsar said.
In its annual report, WPS said it favors replacing the generators, a move that would require the approval of the Wisconsin Public Service Commission.
Kicsar said a decision could be made by the end of 1997.
Kicsar also confirmed other disclosures in the company's annual report.

The company said it expected to spend $74 million on construction projects in 1997, $110 million in 1998 and $74.7 million in 1999. WPS said it needed to make large investments in capital assets used to deliver its electric and natural gas services.

WPS also said it may issue up to $150 million of bonds and debentures and $100 million of common stock in 1998 and 1999. It will use the proceeds to finance expenditures, maturing bonds and for non-regulated projects, WPS said.

Additionally, WPS said environmental cleanup may be needed at eight of its former manufactured gas facilities, at an estimated cost of between $34.7 million and $41.7 million. The cost, expected to be recovered in future customer rates, would be spread out over 32 years, the company said.
WPS shares were off 1/4 at 26-1/2 in midafternoon trading on Thursday.
